questions.question:
A $100$ kg object is projected from a point located $6371$ km from the centre of the Earth.

What is the launch velocity of the projectile so that the velocity would never fall below $2000\ \text{m s}^{-1}$?
questions.answer:
The speed is least as $r \to \infty$, where $U \to 0$. By conservation of energy, require $\tfrac12 mv^2 - \dfrac{GMm}{r} = \tfrac12 m(2000)^2$, so
$$v = \sqrt{v_{esc}^2 + 2000^2},\qquad v_{esc} = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{r}} = \sqrt{\frac{2(6.67\times10^{-11})(6.0\times10^{24})}{6.371\times10^{6}}} \approx 11\,208\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$
$$v = \sqrt{11\,208^2 + 2000^2} \approx 11\,386\ \text{m s}^{-1}. \quad\textbf{(C)}$$
(B) is just the escape velocity; (D) wrongly adds the speeds ($11\,208 + 2000$) instead of the kinetic energies.
